title: Airport ground transport: trips, per-trip fees and the City ledger
question: Do the Airport's trip counts, its per-trip fees and the City ledger agree, and are permitted companies active?
finding: In 256 of 268 permit-type years every month's revenue is the trip count times one fee, so the revenue column is computed from the trip counts. The ledger's ground-transport trip fees run above the trip table every year ($4.9 million more in fiscal 2026, taxis left out of both). Shared-ride vans made 445,519 recorded trips with $21 of per-trip revenue. 37 of 1872 active fleet permits have no active vehicle on file.
how: Trip table (e3x5-4br3) by permit type and Airport fiscal year (July to June); ledger sub-object "Ground Trans Trip Fees" for the Airport (bpnb-jwfb). Active company permits (x2zf-uu4r, status A) joined to active vehicles (p6ht-ubmk, status A) on the permit holder number; ride-hail, autonomous and car-share permits are left out because their vehicles are not listed. The day-permit file is counted only: it names individuals.
limits: The trip table holds no company-level counts, so trips cannot be checked company by company. Shared-ride vans and courtesy shuttles may pay under permit or concession terms rather than per trip; the ledger can include permit, late and application fees that the trip table does not. A permit with no active vehicle can be one between vehicles or awaiting inspection.
